text:
Marta (People Ops): Quick heads-up — we've seen a handful of late review form requests this week (LOA returns, caregiver leaves, and some people who switched teams mid-cycle). We need a crisp SLA + exception flow so calibration doesn't get blocked. Proposed: reviewer SLA = 5 business days; managers can request a 7-day extension via people-ops self-serve; anything >7 days needs Director sign-off + cc to people-ops. Agree?

Ash (Eng Manager): +1 on 5 days. We keep getting stalled calibrations because reviews are missing. One question: can we allow a "partial" review submission if manager can't get full data but can give core bullets?

Pranav (Platform): Also: split-role ICs (eng + platform infra) were inconsistently bucketed last cycle. Do we have guidance for which ladder to evaluate against?

Marta (People Ops): Good points. 1) Partial reviews: yes — add a checkbox "Partial review: core bullets only" and require a short note of what is missing. We'll surface those in calibration so leads know to probe. 2) Split-role guidance: pick the role where the majority of impact happened during the cycle; we'll add a dropdown on the form for Primary role (Eng / Eng-Manager / Platform / Cross-functional).

Dana (People Ops): Exception flow (draft): managers email: people-ops@redwood.com with subject REVIEW EXTENSION <EMPLOYEE NAME> <NEW DATE> and include: reason (LOA/caregiver/other), dates impacted, and requested new due date. People Ops will respond within 24 hours. Here's a paste template: 

Subject: REVIEW EXTENSION — Alex Chen — returning from LOA
Body:
- Employee: Alex Chen (alex@redwood.com)
- Manager: Ash Patel
- Reason: 12-week parental leave; returned 3/12
- Requested new due date: 3/26
- Manager note: will provide condensed bullets; full review expected by 4/9

Sam (Recruiter): One more edge-case: new hires who started within the review window (<60 days). Our past practice was to exclude them from full performance calibration and provide a "onboarding checkpoint" note instead. Can we include an explicit rule in the doc?

Lisa (Director Eng): Yes — be explicit: hires <60 days get an onboarding checkpoint and are not part of calibration buckets. Managers should still submit a short onboarding note for context. Also: if exceptions accumulate and change distribution, calibration leads should flag up to org leadership. Managers — please surface exceptions to calibration leads by EOD Friday.

Ash (Eng Manager): Ack. I'll ping my managers to use the partial-review checkbox and follow the extension template. Two asks: 1) Add the extension count to the Review Ops dashboard, 2) Add a small blurb in the Reviewer guide about balancing partial vs full reviews.

Marta (People Ops): Done — added the extension template and the partial-review checkbox to the review form draft. Updated the Reviewer SLA section in the Review Ops doc: https://redwood.internal/review-ops/exception-flow (will publish tomorrow morning) :tada:

Pranav (Platform): Thanks. Can we also log extension counts in the Console (per team) so we can analyze patterns next retro?

Marta (People Ops): Yup — adding a tracking row for "Extensions requested" + reason buckets (LOA/caregiver/new-hire/team-change). We'll surface a weekly number to calibration leads. Thanks everyone for quick feedback.

Lisa (Director Eng): Appreciate it — please make sure managers see the email tomorrow so calibration isn't held up. :+1:
